input.contents:
---
description: Always tell the user exactly what changed in any CSV file
globs: "**/*.csv"
alwaysApply: true
---

# Report CSV Changes

Whenever you create, edit, fill, restore, or otherwise change any CSV file, always tell the user what changed. Do not skip this even if the change is small.

Include, as applicable:

- Which CSV file(s) were changed (file name/path)
- What was done (rows added, updated, deleted, columns filled, values replaced, backup created, etc.)
- Which rows, SKUs, styles, or records were affected
- Which columns/fields changed
- Before vs after values when specific cells were updated
- How many rows/records were affected
- Any backup file created as part of the change

Give this summary in the reply to the user. Do not only leave it in comments, commit messages, or tool output.

content.text:
Saved. From now on I will always tell you what changed in a CSV.

That includes:

- Which file was changed
- What happened (rows added, updated, deleted, fields filled, restored, etc.)
- Which records/SKUs were affected
- Which columns changed, and before/after values when cells were updated
- How many rows were affected
- Any backup created

This is stored as a project rule, so it will apply in future chats in this workspace.
